title: Rabbi Yannai Ze’ira
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was a priest, as related in [Yerushalmi Berakhot, chapter 3, halakhah 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.3.1.15). When his father-in-law, who was also his teacher, died, he asked Rabbi Yosi whether he might become ritually impure for him, and Rabbi Yosi forbade it. Rabbi Acha heard and said that he might become impure (in [Nazir, chapter 7, halakhah 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nazir.7.1.7), the reading is Rabbi Chama). In [Yerushalmi Shabbat, chapter 6, halakhah 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.6.5.3), Rabbi Yannai Ze’ira’s ear ornaments fell from his ears on Shabbat. He wanted to put them back, but his colleagues rebuked him.[^1] In Taanit, chapter 2, halakhah 6, and at the beginning of Avodah Zarah, chapter 4, Rabbi Yannai Ze’ira speaks in the name of his forebears. It is very likely that the Rabbi Yannai found in the sequence ‘R. Z., Rabbi Yannai, R' Yirmeyah’ in Shabbat, chapter 2, halakhah 3, is Rabbi Yannai Ze’ira.[^2]
Mevo ha-Yerushalmi conjectures that he is Rabbi Yannai son of R' Yannai Saba, mentioned at the end of Megillah.[^3]

notes.text: Hyman’s הטרכין is rendered ‘ear ornaments.’ The Yerushalmi calls the object עודדיה דאודניה and describes the rebuke משום תכשיט, ‘as an ornament’; the precise object is uncertain. Berakhot names Rabbi Acha, while the Nazir parallel has Rabbi Chama.
ר״ז gives an abbreviated name. ‘Forebears’ does not specify an individual father.
Hyman’s final reference, ‘the end of Megillah,’ does not specify which Talmud.
